cases.intent: Repeated commas and whitespace-only ordinary labels are discarded.
Trim ordinary boundary whitespace, collapse internal ordinary runs, and lowercase ASCII letters.
A comma inside quotes is literal, quote delimiters are removed, and adjacent text concatenates.
Quoted and unquoted fragments concatenate when quote delimiters occur within a label.
Escaped comma, quote, and backslash are preserved literally and do not act as delimiters.
Escaped boundary whitespace remains protected with exact content and multiplicity.
Quoted whitespace at label boundaries is preserved rather than trimmed.
Protected whitespace breaks ordinary whitespace runs while each ordinary run collapses independently.
An escaped quote inside quoted mode is literal and a quoted comma remains part of the label.
Lowercase only ASCII A-Z while preserving punctuation and other literal characters.
Normalized duplicate labels are discarded after preserving the first occurrence order.
A label containing only quoted whitespace is nonempty and retained exactly.
Empty labels from separators are discarded while valid labels remain in order.
A trailing unpaired backslash raises ValueError for the whole input even after a valid label.
An unclosed quote raises ValueError for the whole input after an otherwise valid preceding label.
Escaped comma does not split, while a later unescaped comma outside quotes does split.
Ordinary whitespace is trimmed at true boundaries but protected whitespace remains adjacent to content.

rationale: These deterministic cases cover empty input and empty labels, separator handling, quote toggling and adjacency, escaped delimiters and whitespace, ordinary versus protected whitespace normalization, ASCII-only lowercasing, preservation of other characters, deduplication order, whitespace-only protected labels, and whole-input errors for trailing backslashes and unclosed quotes.
